newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS-Czech central bank hikes Lombard rate to 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Czech central bank hikes Lombard rate to 50 pct.

text.p: The Czech central bank (CNB) hiked its Lombard last-resort lending rate to 50 percent from 14 percent on Friday, in an attempt to shore up the sagging crown after several waves of direct intervention failed.
CNB board member Ludek Niedermeyer told Reuters the move was part of a three-pronged strategy in response to short-selling which had pushed the crown to record lows in recent days.

"We are increasing the Lombard rate to 50 percent...with immediate effect," he said. "At the same time, we will restrict the access of the banks to the Lombard window if necessary and we will adequately change the repo rate in our future open market operations," he said.
The Lombard rate is a last-resort lending facility for banks.

"Normally the Lombard rate is not used, but because banks are spending domestic currency and buying foreign currency, there could be a liquidity shortage and in such a circumstance, the central bank is not very happy to provide financing of speculation against the domestic currency," he added.

The Czech crown has been heavily pressured over the past week as mainly foreign investors pushed the currency lower, hitting a record weak point of five percent on the depreciation side of its dollar/mark basket parity, prompting the CNB to intervene on the market for the first time in over a year.

But the interventions over two days failed to scare off market bears who continued to push the crown lower and analysts said stronger action was needed if the crown was to claw its way back toward parity.

Niedermeyer said the third stage of the strategy could involve a further raising of the repo rate -- which was hiked 50 basis points to 12.9 percent earlier on Friday -- depending on market conditions.

"It will depend on the concrete situation on the money market and forex market on Monday morning," he said. "We expect that after some wave of short-selling is over, then we will not need extremely high interest rates, but we are ready to use them if the market is volatile," Niedermeyer added.
The crown firmed immediately after Niedermeyer's statement to about minus 3.0 percent to its parity rate at 1430 GMT, from minus 4.19 percent just before he spoke.
In explaining why the CNB entered the market in the first place, Vice-governor Jan Vit blamed the crown's fall on developments on financial markets abroad and not domestic economic factors.
He did not elaborate, but some traders said foreign investors were getting nervous over some emerging market economies troubled by a weak external position, such as Thailand.
